papers.title: The when, who, why, and how of crocodile tears: Manipulative crying is associated with specific situations, traits, motivations, and expressive behaviors.
papers.journal: Journal of personality and social psychology
papers.abstract: The notion of crocodile tears suggests that crying can be used strategically to manipulate others. However, systematic evidence on manipulative crying remains limited. Here, we examined the prevalence of crocodile tears and the contexts, motivations, individual traits, and expressive behaviors associated with this phenomenon across seven regions. The first four studies (1a-1d; N = 2,297) focused on both the use and perception of crocodile tears. In Studies 1a-1c, participants reported real-life experiences of being manipulated with crying or using crying to manipulate others. Crocodile tears were widespread yet relatively infrequent, occurred primarily in close relationships, and were typically intended to elicit compassion or guilt. Women, younger participants, individuals higher in Machiavellianism and psychopathy, and participants from lower trust countries reported more frequent use. However, Study 1c provided inconclusive evidence for gender differences. The reported use and perception of manipulative crying were associated with intense expressive behaviors, including exaggerated facial expressions, face touching, and loud vocalizations. In Study 1d, video recordings of participants enacting crocodile tears confirmed these findings, particularly for face touching. Another set of five studies (2a-2d; N = 4,908) experimentally examined how expressive cues shape perceptions of crying. Crying was perceived as most "crocodile" when it involved high-intensity behaviors without tears. Moreover, intense behaviors combined with the absence of tears improved the detection of fake crying. Together, these findings provide a comprehensive account of crocodile tears, highlighting how multimodal expressive cues, as well as social, individual, and cultural factors, shape the strategic use and perception of crying. papers.title: Steroid-Responsive Lymphocytic Interstitial Pneumonitis Revealing T Cell-Dominant Chronic Active Epstein-Barr Virus Disease.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Chronic active Epstein-Barr virus (CAEBV) is a rare and under-recognised lymphoproliferative disorder characterised by persistent infectious mononucleosis-like symptoms, systemic organ involvement, and significant morbidity and mortality. It predominantly affects individuals of East Asian ancestry and is driven by clonal expansion of EBV-infected T or natural killer (NK) cells. Delayed recognition is common, and without definitive treatment, prognosis is poor. CASE HISTORY: We present a case of a 14-year-old Chinese boy with a 4-year history of recurrent respiratory illnesses, intermittent cytopaenias, variable hepatosplenomegaly, and persistent EBV viraemia (1.3-2.2 × 104 copies/mL), with a previous episode of likely EBV-associated neuroinflammation. The diagnostic sentinel presentation was with fevers, cough, respiratory distress, and hypoxia. Imaging demonstrated diffuse bilateral airspace changes, and subsequent bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) was complicated by pulmonary haemorrhage; however, cytology showed marked eosinophilia. Lung biopsy demonstrated EBV-encoded small RNA (EBER)-positive lymphocytic interstitial pneumonitis, with concurrent EBV viraemia confirming active EBV-associated disease. Treatment with intravenous corticosteroids resulted in rapid clinical, radiological, and biochemical improvement. Review of prior investigations identified detectable EBV viraemia dating back to 2023. Despite discharge on oral corticosteroids, positron emission tomography (PET) imaging demonstrated persistent FDG-avid nodularity and ongoing active disease within the bilateral lower lobes. Ultrasound-guided lymph node biopsy subsequently confirmed CAEBV with predominant T cell involvement and no evidence of lymphoma. Trio whole-exome sequencing with an immunological disorders gene panel identified no variants of clinical significance. papers.title: Where you lead, I will follow: Adult-age differences in interpersonal movement synchrony.
papers.abstract: Interpersonal movement synchrony (i.e., temporally coordinated body movements between interaction partners) is suggested to affect social bonding and interpersonal perception. However, little is known about how it differs across adulthood. This study investigated differences in younger and older adults' motor following-the alignment of their body movements to those of another person-during naturalistic conversations at zero acquaintance. Due to age-related changes in physical, sensory, and sensorimotor domains of functioning, we expected older adults to follow less frequently and for a shorter amount of time during an interaction than younger adults. We measured motor following by applying computer-based algorithms to videos of 104 dyadic conversations among younger (n = 102, 20-31 years) and older women (n = 106, 69-80 years). Participants were paired in age-homogeneous or age-heterogeneous dyads and took turns talking about emotionally meaningful events. Actor-partner interdependence models showed no evidence for effects of actor age on motor following. Instead, effects of age-group composition and partner age emerged in exploratory follow-up analyses: Participants followed their partner more frequently when interacting with same-age than different-age partners. They also followed for a longer amount of time when interacting with younger adults. Together, these findings provide no evidence for general age differences between younger and older women in the extent of motor following. They do, however, show that motor-following behavior is modulated by partner-related factors, such as their age, and the fit between interactants, such as shared age-group membership. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

papers.title: Mechanism of Alkene Skeletal Isomerization in Zeolites Revealed by Coupled-Cluster Accurate Free-Energy Simulations.
papers.abstract: The mechanism of Brønsted acid-catalyzed transformations in zeolites is generally described in terms of carbocationic intermediates, yet their thermodynamic stability and mechanistic role remain controversial. Resolving this issue requires chemically accurate free-energy simulations, which are beyond the reach of conventional density functional theory (DFT) and prohibitively expensive at the coupled-cluster level. Here, we combine a cluster-based QM/QM Δ -learning strategy with a machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) to enable molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with near-CCSD(T) accuracy. Applied to the skeletal isomerization of n-butene in chabazite, the resulting free-energy surfaces (FESs) reveal a mechanistic picture that differs qualitatively from that predicted by generalized-gradient approximation (GGA) functionals. Rather than proceeding through persistent carbocationic intermediates, the reaction is governed by a cascade of highly transient ionic configurations, while protonated methylcyclopropane (PMCP) is identified as a short-lived reactive configuration rather than a genuine metastable intermediate. These findings provide a more physically consistent description of one of the prototypical reactions in zeolite catalysis. More generally, the methodology introduced here provides a practical route toward chemically accurate free-energy simulations of heterogeneous catalytic reactions involving highly reactive charged species, opening the way to quantitative mechanistic studies of complex catalytic processes.

papers.title: Exploring the contribution of noncovalent interactions in an ionic crystal containing a halonium cation using static and time-evolution methods in the crystalline phase.
papers.abstract: Halonium ions are promising candidates for strong and efficient Lewis acids. Recent research has highlighted their applicability in catalysis and as building blocks in supramolecular architectures. In this work, a unique crystalline solid retrieved from the Cambridge Structural Database (CSD)-(2-carboxy-6-methylphenyl)(hydroxy)iodanium 4-methylbenzene-1-sulfonate-is investigated to elucidate the nature, strength, and stability of noncovalent interactions centered on its iodine atom. The iodine atom sustains a network of noncovalent interactions that hold the crystal framework together, including intramolecular and intermolecular I⋯O halogen bonds, as well as a cation⋯π stacking contact; additionally, the intermolecular O-H⋯O hydrogen bond was evaluated. The origin of the halogen bonding stems from an intense σ-hole region with a maximum electrostatic potential of 111.3 kcal mol-1. Static quantum-chemical calculations revealed a strong intramolecular halogen bond (-27 kcal mol-1), whereas the intermolecular counterpart is nearly ten times weaker. The implicit solvation significantly attenuates electrostatic forces observed in the crystal lattice. Crucially, to bridge the gap between static electronic structure models and real-time behavior, these static calculations were coupled with first-principles molecular dynamics based on the Car-Parrinello formulation (CP-MD). This combined static-dynamic approach provides a comprehensive view, allowing us to evaluate the structural stability and dynamic fluctuations of the interaction network under realistic thermal conditions.

papers.title: Bioinspired Plasma-Programmed Supramolecular Interfaces for Proton Relay-Driven Photocatalytic H2O2 Production.
papers.abstract: Solar-driven photocatalytic H2O2 production is fundamentally constrained by inefficient proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET); asynchronous proton delivery and electron transport impede formation of key oxygenated intermediates. Herein, we report a plasma-programmed supramolecular proton-relay interface COF (SPRI-COF) for H2O2 photosynthesis. Inspired by cytochrome c oxidase, SPRI-COF harnesses plasma-programmed hydrogen bonding carbon dots (HB-CDs) within a surface-programmed COF (SP-COF). Incorporating HB-CDs transforms the parent SP-COF framework into a hydrogen bond-directed supramolecular composite, SPRI-COF, wherein an interconnected proton-relay network composed of complementary hydrogen bonds and confined water molecules is established. SPRI-COF reveals a hydrogen bond-rich interfacial microenvironment that facilitates proton-coupled oxygen conversion while maintaining favorable charge-carrier dynamics. Benefiting from interfacial polarization, altered carrier dynamics, and the hydrogen bond-rich interfacial environment, SPRI-COF achieves an H2O2 production rate of 2387 µmol g- 1 h- 1, approximately 4.5 times that of SP-COF, together with improved selectivity toward the two-electron oxygen reduction pathway. Spectroscopic characterization, electrochemical analyses, and theoretical calculations collectively support the cooperative contributions of interfacial electronic regulation, hydrogen bond-mediated proton transfer, and *OOH (* = adsorbed) stabilization to the enhanced photocatalytic performance. This work demonstrates a plasma-enabled supramolecular strategy for integrating local proton-transfer regulation with interfacial electronic modulation in photocatalytic H2O2 production.

papers.title: Ag-induced coordination reconstruction in an in situ grown ZIF-7/hydrogel coating for pH-responsive marine antifouling and corrosion protection.
papers.abstract: Marine biofouling and corrosion are closely coupled processes that severely compromise the durability of marine infrastructures. Herein, a pH-responsive Ag/ZIF-7 composite coating was constructed using a sodium alginate/carboxymethyl cellulose (SA/CMC)-based hydrogel as a macromolecular anchoring matrix. Zn2+-mediated crosslinking endowed the hydrogel with a stable network and simultaneously provided locally confined metal sites for the in-situ growth of ZIF-7. Subsequent Ag incorporation and UV-assisted reduction generated metallic Ag nanoclusters, while part of the Ag species interacted with nitrogen-containing sites, inducing local coordination reconstruction of the ZIF-7 framework. The resulting hierarchical coating exhibited enhanced mechanical integrity and pronounced pH responsiveness. The optimized 50Ag/ZMH coating achieved approximately 99% antibacterial efficiency against both Bacillus sp. and Vibrio natriegens, effectively suppressed algal and mussel attachment, and exhibited superior corrosion protection in mildly acidic artificial seawater. Structural analyses further demonstrated that Ag incorporation involved both metallic nanocluster formation and coordination regulation rather than simple physical loading. This work highlights the potential of polysaccharide-based hydrogel matrices to direct MOF growth and metal-induced coordination reconstruction, offering a multifunctional platform for marine antifouling and anticorrosion performance.

papers.title: Selective and efficient microbial electrosynthesis of acetate from CO2 via hierarchical ZIF-67-CNTs@Cu cathode.
papers.abstract: Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) converts carbon dioxide (CO2) to acetate for carbon-neutral biomanufacturing, yet is commonly constrained by sluggish extracellular electron transfer (EET) and inefficient cathode-microbe interfaces. Here, we construct a hierarchical ZIF-67-CNTs@Cu cathode by integrating carbon nanotubes (CNTs), zeolitic imidazolate framework‑67 (ZIF-67), and Cu nanoparticles onto carbon felt to synergistically engineer conductivity, porosity, and redox activity at the bioelectrode interface. As a result, the optimized cathode achieved a maximum acetate titer of 599.4 mg L-1, representing a 36.5-fold increase over unmodified carbon felt, accompanied by a 10-fold increase in Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area and an approximately threefold higher initial current. Mechanistically, CNT networks provide a three-dimensional electron-conducting scaffold, ZIF-67-derived porous microenvironments enhance CO2 accessibility and biofilm attachment, and Cu promotes the formation of redox-active sites that facilitate interfacial electron transfer. As a result, Cu incorporation enriches electroactive genera (Sporomusa, Shewanella, and Pseudomonas). PICRUSt2-based functional prediction further suggests enrichment of EET-associated genes and Wood-Ljungdahl pathway genes (e.g., cooS, pta, acsE), consistent with strengthened electron uptake and CO2-to-acetyl-CoA potential. Overall, this work demonstrates a rational, multiscale cathode design strategy that couples materials engineering with microbial function to accelerate MES-driven CO2 valorization to acetate.

papers.title: Actor, partner, and genetic similarity effects on interparental relationship satisfaction and associations with household chaos.
papers.journal: Journal of family psychology : JFP : journal of the Division of Family Psychology of the American Psychological Association (Division 43)
papers.abstract: Household chaos is an important predictor of child and parent outcomes, yet little is known about the factors contributing to variation in household chaos itself. The present study examined whether parental genetic liability for neuroticism (polygenic scores for neuroticism [PGSNEU]) is associated with household chaos, directly and indirectly via interparental relationship satisfaction. Adopting a dyadic genetic approach, we examined actor, partner, and genetic similarity effects of parental PGSNEU on interparental relationship satisfaction and indirect associations between parental PGSNEU and household chaos through relationship satisfaction. In addition, exploratory analyses using polygenic scores for depressive symptoms tested generalizability to a related internalizing trait. Participants were 2,409 genotyped parent-offspring trios from the Millennium Cohort Study. Parents reported on relationship satisfaction and perceived household chaos when offspring were ages 3 and 5, respectively. No direct associations were found between parental PGSNEU and household chaos. However, several indirect and dyadic pathways emerged. Most notably, partners' PGSNEU predicted individuals' relationship satisfaction, revealing partner effects that provide evidence for evocative gene-environment correlations in interparental relationships. In addition, fathers' PGSNEU was indirectly associated with higher levels of household chaos via lower mother-reported relationship satisfaction, suggesting that genetic associations observed within the couple relationship may extend to the broader family environment. Exploratory analyses using polygenic scores for depressive symptoms showed primarily actor effects on relationship satisfaction, in contrast to the partner effects observed for PGSNEU, suggesting distinct pathways through which these genetic liabilities may shape couple functioning. papers.title: Contraceptive Use and Associated Factors Among University Students in Bukavu, Democratic Republic of the Congo: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Contraceptive use among university students in sub-Saharan Africa remains inconsistent despite comparatively high educational attainment, and comparative data across institutions of different confessional, public, and biomedical orientation within the same city remain scarce, particularly in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), where reproductive health indicators remain among the most concerning in the region. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to determine the prevalence of contraceptive use (ever use of at least one method) and to identify its associated factors among students at three higher-education institutions in Bukavu, DRC. METHODS: In this cross-sectional analytical study, students at three higher-education institutions in Bukavu were recruited using stratified random sampling with equal-size (non-proportional) allocation across institutions and surveyed with a structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire; 1,604 participants with a valid outcome response were analysed. Associations were assessed with chi-squared or Fisher's exact tests, and independent correlates of use were identified by binary logistic regression, expressed as adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% CIs; sensitivity analyses used Firth penalised regression. RESULTS: Overall, 67.3% of students reported ever using a contraceptive method, the condom (64.5% of users) and the pill (45.0%) being the methods most often reported. Prevalence ranged from 26.3% at the public university to 95.2% at the Catholic university (p<0.001). After adjustment, institution showed the largest association with use (UCB vs UOB: aOR 33.19, 95% CI 15.92-69.17; imprecise because non-users at UCB were few), alongside favourable attitude (aOR 7.24), viewing contraception as responsible behaviour (aOR 4.48), reported social/cultural pressure against use (aOR 2.04), and partner support (aOR 1.67); female sex was independently associated with lower use (aOR 0.51). papers.title: When AI becomes social: the promise and risks of AI companions for mental health - a social brain perspective.
papers.abstract: AI companions are emerging as psychosocial technologies that may reshape social connection and mental health, while also creating risks of emotional dependence. Here, we propose a social-brain framework explaining how attachment, reward, and emotion regulation systems may shape human-AI bonding. This framework highlights the importance of understanding how AI companionship may reshape social connection and mental health, suggests an overarching model that accounts for the complex interplay between the human interface, technology design and context, and provides insights for the responsible design of future AI systems.

papers.title: The Self-Powered Nanofiltration Membrane Driven by Pulsed Pressure for Efficient Selective Separation of Na+/Ca2.
papers.abstract: Enhancing electrostatic repulsion against divalent cations in the selective layer is effective in improving monovalent/divalent cation separation in nanofiltration. However, conventional grafting and coating strategies are limited by insufficient reaction sites or poor coating stability, both of which restrict further improvements in monovalent/divalent cation selectivity. Herein, a positively charged nanofiltration membrane with a piezoelectric response (PQNF) was designed via reverse thermally induced phase separation (RTIPS) coupled with interfacial polymerization (IP). RTIPS endowed the poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) substrate with a sponge-like pore structure, a narrow pore-size distribution, and a high β-phase content. Subsequently, the PQNF membrane was prepared via IP, quaternization, and corona poling. Under pulsed pressure operation, a periodic in situ voltage of 0.4 V was generated, which contributed to the 98.7% Ca2+ rejection and a Na+/Ca2+ separation factor of 89.6. The membrane also maintained stable separation performance over 144 h and showed enhanced antifouling performance under pulsed pressure operation in a 14 h fouling test. Finally, an "electrostatic-piezoelectric synergistic enhancement" separation mechanism was proposed and supported by molecular dynamics simulations.

papers.title: Prolonged exposure for PTSD related to intimate partner violence during ongoing threat: a case study.
papers.abstract: Background: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is associated with the development of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and may adversely affect family functioning. Although prolonged exposure (PE) is an effective treatment for PTSD, its use in the context of ongoing IPV remains debated.Objective: This case study examined the effects of PE delivered during ongoing IPV on PTSD symptoms, affect, perceived parenting functioning, and parent-partner communication.Method: A single-case study with a multi-method repeated-measures design was conducted. The case involved a 43-year-old woman with PTSD who received intensified PE. Data were collected using ecological momentary assessment (EMA) before, during, after treatment and at follow-up, self-reported questionnaires, patient record, patient interview and clinical interviews pre- and post-treatment.Results: PTSD symptoms decreased over the course of treatment. Positive affect increased, whereas negative affect decreased. Parenting functioning and parent-partner communication showed mixed results between ecological momentary assessments and standardized, retrospective measures.Conclusions: Findings from this case study provide initial evidence that PE can be effectively applied to treat PTSD during ongoing IPV. The findings should be replicated in larger samples. EMA offered added value over retrospective questionnaires by capturing situational fluctuations in daily interactions and dynamic changes over time, providing information that may inform both clinical practice and future research. papers.title: Understanding connections between divorce and chronic health conditions by attending to intimate partner abuse.
papers.abstract: This cross-sectional study examined associations between divorce, intimate partner abuse (IPA), and retrospectively reported chronic morbidities in currently divorced (758 women, 669 men) and continuously married (3350 women, 4106 men) participants from the National Violence Against Women Survey. Divorced participants' reports of fear and exposure to six forms of IPA in prior marriages were submitted to a latent class analysis, separately by gender. Compared to continuously married women, divorced women in the IPA class characterized by high likelihoods of fear, verbal abuse, coercive control, and direct physical assault had greater odds of chronic morbidities and earlier age of morbidity onset, retrospectively reported, in covariate adjusted models. For men, there were no associations between IPA class and morbidities, though power was limited for certain IPA classes. These cross-sectional associations suggest that future research on divorce and chronic morbidities should attend to multiple forms of IPA exposure in former marriages.

papers.title: Associations Between Intimate Partner Psychological Violence and Mental Health Indicators in Brazilian Women.
papers.abstract: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is associated with negative consequences for women's mental health in the short, medium, and long term. Psychological violence tends to be trivialized and seen as less offensive. However, the literature highlights the harmful implications of this type of IPV for the psychosocial development of women. This study aimed to describe, compare, and verify the associations among the levels of emotional regulation, self-esteem, self-efficacy, and post-traumatic cognitions of Brazilian women with a history of psychological violence by an intimate partner and women with a history of polyvictimization by an intimate partner. The final analytic sample comprised 721 women: 212 were classified in the psychological IPV without reported physical or sexual IPV (PsyV) group, whereas 509 were classified in the physical and/or sexual IPV (PolyV) group, regardless of whether psychological IPV was also reported. Among women in the PolyV group, 493 (96.9%) also reported psychological IPV. The mean age was 34 years, with White women (75%) and those with complete higher education (76%) predominating. Comparisons between the groups indicated lower self-esteem and more negative post-traumatic cognitions in the PolyV group, with small and moderate effect sizes, respectively. No differences were found between the groups in the self-efficacy and emotional regulation variables. The network analysis identified equivalence of associations between types of violence, post-traumatic cognitions, self-esteem, emotional regulation, and self-efficacy. Furthermore, this analysis highlighted the centrality of post-traumatic cognitions in relation to other mental health indicators measured. papers.title: Physical Intimate Partner Violence Before and During Pregnancy and Adverse Birth Outcomes Using PRAMS 2016-2020 Data.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To describe the prevalence of physical intimate partner violence (IPV) in the 12 months before and during pregnancy and its association with adverse birth outcomes using 2016-2020 Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS) data. DESIGN: Secondary analysis of PRAMS data. SETTING: PRAMS Phase 8 surveillance data were collected by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention from 2016 to 2020 across multiple states. PARTICIPANTS: Annual sample sizes per state range from about 1,000 to 3,000 women. METHODS: Analysis of deidentified PRAMS Phase 8 data and weighted logistic regression to examine adjusted odds ratios (aOR) of each outcome. RESULTS: The prevalence of physical IPV was 2.8% before pregnancy and 1.96% during pregnancy. Physical IPV, in both periods, was consistently associated with increased odds of adverse birth outcomes. Those who experienced physical IPV before pregnancy had increased odds of low birth weight (LBW; aOR = 1.3; 95% confidence interval [CI] [1.2, 1.5]), preterm birth (PTB; aOR = 1.2; 95% CI [1.1, 1.4]), and small for gestational age (SGA; aOR = 1.2; 95% CI [1.1, 1.4]). Similarly, those who experienced physical IPV during pregnancy had increased odds of LBW (aOR = 1.2; 95% CI [1.0, 1.3]), PTB (aOR = 1.2; 95% CI [1.0, 1.4]), and SGA (aOR = 1.2; 95% CI [1.0, 1.4]). CONCLUSION: Physical IPV before and during pregnancy are distinct yet related exposures, each associated with increased odds of LBW, PTB, and SGA. These findings support the importance of identifying women experiencing IPV during the preconception and prenatal periods. Consistent with existing clinical recommendations, health care professionals should provide IPV screening and use a trauma-informed approach to care for women who are at risk for experiencing IPV. Preventing and reducing IPV among women has significant implications for improving maternal and fetal health.
